'''Dynamic Encryption''' is a cryptographic principle that enables two parties to change the encryption algorithm for every transaction.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Dynamic Encryption|first=Lars |last=Ramkilde Knudsen|journal=Journal of Cyber Security and Mobility|year=2015|volume=3|issue=4|pages=357–370|doi=10.13052/jcsm2245-1439.341|s2cid=40910779|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://larsrknudsen.wordpress.com/2019/01/10/38/ |title=Blog post on Dynamic Encryption |first=Lars |last=Ramkilde Knudsen|date=10 January 2019 }}</ref>

== Introduction ==

The principle of Dynamic Encryption was invented by Professor [[Lars Ramkilde Knudsen|Lars R. Knudsen]] at the [[Technical University of Denmark]]. The Dynamic Encryption principle is patented.

In traditional cryptosystems a specific cipher is chosen thus security of the system relies on the frequency of key changes and the key agreement scheme. Dynamic Encryption enhance such a system by defining a set of ciphers such that not only the key but also the cipher changes on every new data transaction. Which follows the motivation of the Moving Target Defense paradigm.

In order to establish an encrypted channel using the Dynamic Encryption principle the sender and receiver first negotiates a key and then the sender picks a cipher from a large pool of ciphers and sends that together with the encrypted message.

It is possible to construct a dynamic encryption system, from known ciphers (such as [[Advanced Encryption Standard|AES]], [[Data Encryption Standard|DES]], etc.), such that all encryption algorithms generated from this system are at least as secure as the static underlying cipher.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dencrypt.dk/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/Dencrypt-Vincent-Rijmen.pdf |title=Opinion on Dynamic Encryption |first=Vincent |last=Rijmen}}</ref>

== Details ==

The exchanged cryptosystems do not have to be kept secret, but to avoid attackers modifying the transmitted encryption systems, the system should be transmitted over an authenticated channel.

== Applications ==

Dynamic Encryption is deployed by Dencrypt Talk, a voice communication and live-chat application for iOS and Android.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ia.nato.int/niapc/Product/Dencrypt-Talk_723|title=Dencrypt Talk|publisher=[[NATO]]}}</ref> Dencrypt Talk applies the principle by wrapping standard AES encryption with a dynamic layer which is changed for every phone call between two clients.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dencrypt.dk/dencrypt-talk/|title=Dencrypt Talk|publisher=Dencrypt A/S}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dtu.dk/english/news/2014/10/dynamic-encryption-keeps-secrets?id=24491899-d1af-4620-a43a-ae524a36bdab|title=Dynamic Encryption keeps secrets|publisher=[[Technical University of Denmark]]}}</ref>

== Awards ==

In 2017, Dencrypt won NATO's Defence Innovation Challenge award in recognition of their deployment of Dynamic Encryption for voice communication.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dtu.dk/english/News/2017/05/Encryption-company-wins-NATO-innovation-award?id=3304ea1a-db2d-456d-abbc-bc0ce9aa1dcd|title=Encryption company wins NATO innovation award|publisher=[[Technical University of Denmark]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nitec.nato.int/wp-content/uploads/2018/01/NITEC-17-Report.pdf|title=NITEC '17 Report|publisher=[[NATO]]|access-date=2019-06-12|archive-date=2019-05-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190511181022/http://www.nitec.nato.int/wp-content/uploads/2018/01/NITEC-17-Report.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>
